t.1.115.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the sons of Kuntī and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra had been born, the daughter of the king of the Madras spoke these words to Pāṇḍu in private.
t.1.115.2: I feel no anguish on your account, scorcher of foes, even though you are without strength, nor over my always having held the lower rank, sinless one, though I was worthy of the higher.
t.1.115.3: And likewise, O king, on hearing that a hundred sons had been born to Gāndhārī, I did not feel such sorrow, O delight of the Kurus.
t.1.115.4: But this is my great sorrow: that though we are equal, I am without a son. Yet by good fortune my husband now has offspring, at least through Kuntī.
t.1.115.6: Because I am her co-wife, I feel a hesitancy to speak to the daughter of Kunti. But if you are pleased with me, urge her yourself.
t.1.115.5: But if the daughter of the Kunti king would bring about a line of offspring for me, that would be a favor to me, and it would also be for your good.
t.1.115.8: But now that I know this wish of yours, I shall make an effort from here on; I am certain that she, when spoken to by me, will accept my words.
t.1.115.7: Pāṇḍu said: This very matter, Mādrī, constantly turns over in my heart as well; but I could not bring myself to speak to you of it, uncertain whether my words would be welcome or unwelcome to you.
t.1.115.9: Then Pāṇḍu again spoke these words to Kuntī in private: "Bring about the continuation of my lineage, and do what is dear to the world."
t.1.115.10: So that I, our forefathers, and you yourself may not be left without the funeral offerings of rice-balls, and for my sake as well, O blessed lady, do this most excellent good deed.
t.1.115.12: So too, O beautiful lady, brahmins learned in the mantras, having practised exceedingly difficult austerities, approach their gurus for the sake of glory.
t.1.115.11: And for the sake of glory you too must perform this most difficult deed, for even Indra, having attained sovereignty, offered sacrifices out of desire for glory.
t.1.115.13: Likewise all the royal sages, and the brahmins rich in austerity, performed deeds of every kind, high and low, difficult to accomplish, for the sake of glory.
t.1.115.14: So you, O blameless one, carry this Mādrī across as if by a raft; by sharing your offspring with her, attain the highest renown.
t.1.115.15: Thus addressed, she said to Mādrī: "Think once of a deity; from that one you will without doubt have offspring worthy of you."
t.1.115.16: Then Mādrī, after due reflection, went in her mind to the two Aśvins; and they, having come, begot on her twin sons.
t.1.115.17: In the same way, a bodiless voice spoke concerning the twins, Nakula and Sahadeva, who were unequalled in beauty upon the earth.
t.1.115.18: These two, endowed with beauty, strength and virtues, shine exceedingly beyond other people through their splendor and the wealth of their beauty.
t.1.115.19: The dwellers of Śataśṛṅga gave them their names, O lord of the people, with devotion and with due rites, and likewise with blessings.
t.1.115.20: They called the eldest "Yudhiṣṭhira," the middle one "Bhīmasena," and the third "Arjuna"; thus they named the sons of Kuntī.
t.1.115.21: The brahmins, glad at heart, named the two sons of Mādrī, calling the elder Nakula and the other Sahadeva. Those best of the Kurus were born one year after another.
t.1.115.22: Then Pāṇḍu once again urged Kuntī on Mādrī's behalf. Addressed in private, O king, Pṛthā, ever virtuous, said to him:
t.1.115.23: Told to use it only once, she obtained a pair, and by that I have been tricked. I fear being humiliated by her; such is the way of women.
t.1.115.25: Thus were born the five sons of Pāṇḍu, given by the gods, mighty in strength; those glorious ones were the increasers of the Kuru lineage.
t.1.115.24: Foolish as I was, I did not know that invoking a pair would bring a double fruit. Therefore I should not be enjoined by you again; let this be my boon.
t.1.115.26: Endowed with auspicious marks, pleasing to behold like the moon, proud as lions, great archers, moving with the bold stride of lions, lion-necked, those lords of men, mighty as gods, grew up.
t.1.115.27: Growing up there on the holy Himālayan mountain, they filled the great seers who had assembled with wonder.
t.1.115.28: And those five, and the hundred as well, all of them increasers of the Kuru lineage, grew up in a short time, like lotuses in the waters.
